seoTitle: How to Add Jotform to WordPress Easily
metaDescription: Learn how to embed a Jotform form into a WordPress page in 2026 using the Gutenberg editor's Custom HTML block and a copied embed code.
intro: Embedding a Jotform form into a self-hosted WordPress site doesn't require a plugin if you're comfortable with a quick code snippet and the Gutenberg editor. This guide covers copying the right embed code from Jotform's publish panel and pasting it into a Custom HTML block so the form renders responsively on your page.

steps.heading: Open the Publish panel in Jotform
steps.body: Go to your form workspace and navigate to the Publish panel.

steps.heading: Copy the embed code
steps.body: Select the Embed Options tab and copy the source code, choosing between standard JavaScript, a responsive iFrame, or a plug-in key.

steps.heading: Open your WordPress page
steps.body: Log into your WordPress admin panel and open the target page or post in the block editor.

steps.heading: Add a Custom HTML block
steps.body: Click the plus icon to add a new Gutenberg block, then search for and select the Custom HTML or Shortcode block tool.

steps.heading: Paste, adjust, and publish
steps.body: Paste your Jotform embed code into the block, adjust alignment settings to match your theme's margins, then click Update to publish and verify the live front-end view.

faq.question: Do I need a WordPress plugin to embed a Jotform form?
faq.answer: No, pasting the embed code into a Custom HTML block in the Gutenberg editor works without installing a dedicated plugin.

faq.question: Which embed code option should I choose, JavaScript or iFrame?
faq.answer: A responsive iFrame is generally a safer default for compatibility with WordPress themes, while the JavaScript embed can offer tighter visual integration.

faq.question: Will the embedded form resize correctly on mobile devices?
faq.answer: Yes, choosing the responsive iFrame option and verifying the live front-end view helps ensure the form displays properly across devices.

faq.question: Can I embed the same form on multiple WordPress pages?
faq.answer: Yes, you can paste the same embed code into a Custom HTML block on as many pages as you need.
